requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'TokenDance: Scaling Multi-Agent LLM Serving via Collective KV Cache Sharing' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The hardware, software stack, models, and base serving systems (vLLM, LMCache, CacheBlend) required to run TokenDance and its baselines are available and correctly configured.
The GPU hardware environment matches the paper's evaluation setup so that measured latency and memory numbers are comparable.
Code has been implemented to run all experiments on an NVIDIA A100 GPU with 80 GB of memory, matching the hardware used in Section 6.1.

verification.spec: Run nvidia-smi and parse output; assert at least one GPU is present with device name containing 'A100' and total memory >= 80GB (81920 MiB, allow >= 80000 MiB). Also assert CUDA is available via torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0).total_memory >= 80*1024**3 * 0.98.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CUDA toolkit and NVIDIA driver versions installed in the environment are compatible with A100-80GB, FlashAttention, and the vLLM release used as the serving base.

verification.spec: Run `nvidia-smi` and `nvcc --version`; assert an A100-80GB is visible, CUDA driver >= 525, and CUDA toolkit is one of the versions supported by the target vLLM release (e.g., 12.1). Then `python -c 'import torch; assert torch.cuda.is_available()'`.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B model weights and tokenizer are downloaded and loadable by the serving stack.
Code has been implemented to acquire the Qwen2.5-7B model checkpoint and tokenizer and load it into vLLM for inference on a single A100-80GB GPU.

verification.spec: Run a script that instantiates vLLM with Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on a single A100-80GB GPU, loads the tokenizer, and performs a short generation (e.g., 'Hello' prompt with max_tokens=8). Verify: (1) model weights load successfully, (2) tokenizer decodes/encodes a sample string round-trip, (3) generation returns non-empty output, (4) GPU memory usage after load is reported and non-zero.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to acquire the Qwen2.5-14B model checkpoint and tokenizer and load it into vLLM for inference on a single A100-80GB GPU.

verification.spec: Run a script that instantiates vLLM with Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on a single A100-80GB GPU, loads the tokenizer, and performs a short generation (e.g., 'Hello' prompt with max_tokens=8). Verify: (1) model weights load successfully within 80GB memory budget, (2) tokenizer round-trip works on a sample string, (3) generation returns non-empty output, (4) GPU memory usage after load is reported and non-zero.

sub_tasks.requirements: The tokenizer is configured to recognize the reserved <TTSEP> separator token used by the round-aware prompt interface, either through added special tokens or a documented equivalent, so segment boundaries survive tokenization.

verification.spec: Load the tokenizer used by the serving stack, add <TTSEP> as a special token if not present, and tokenize 'A<TTSEP>B'. Assert the resulting token id sequence contains exactly one occurrence of the reserved <TTSEP> id and that it is not split into sub-pieces.

sub_tasks.requirements: Build tooling and code integration for the TokenDance implementation (approximately 3K Python LOC and 500 CUDA/C++ LOC) is in place so the four subsystems can be compiled and loaded together.

Code has been implemented so that the CUDA/C++ extension containing the paired K/V diff kernel and the single-plane diff kernel used by the fused sparse restore path builds successfully and is importable from Python at runtime.

verification.spec: Build the CUDA/C++ extension (e.g., `pip install -e .` or `python setup.py build_ext --inplace`) and then `python -c 'import tokendance._C as ext; assert hasattr(ext, "apply_kv_diff") and hasattr(ext, "apply_kv_diff_paired")'` succeeds with return code 0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Python package layout wires together round-aware segment indexing, collective KV cache reuse, diff-aware storage, and fused sparse restore as distinct modules that can be enabled or disabled independently for baseline comparisons.

verification.spec: Use importlib to import the four modules (round-aware segment indexing, collective KV cache reuse, diff-aware storage, fused sparse restore) as separate submodules. Verify each exposes an enable/disable flag or constructor argument and can be toggled independently in a config object without cross-import errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: A configuration mechanism (e.g., CLI flags or config file) selects between the four evaluated systems (vLLM prefix caching, CacheBlend Ordinary Path, CacheBlend with full recovery, and TokenDance) so that a single driver can run all baselines against the same workload traces.

verification.spec: Invoke the main serving driver with `--system vllm_prefix`, `--system cacheblend_ordinary`, `--system cacheblend_full`, and `--system tokendance` on the same tiny trace. Assert all four return exit code 0 and log the selected system name matching the flag.

sub_tasks.requirements: Runtime configuration exposes the knobs and telemetry the evaluation requires (round latency, KV cache footprint, restore overhead, agent count and QPS sweeps).
Code has been implemented to configure block/chunk size for the segment-based hash table and diff storage so that block granularity is set to 32 tokens, matching the Section 6.4 measurements.

verification.spec: Import the TokenDance configuration module and inspect the block/chunk size constant used for segment-based hashing and diff storage. Assert that the configured value equals 32 tokens per block. Additionally, grep the source for the block size constant and verify a single canonical definition set to 32.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to allow decoding temperature to be fixed at 0 (greedy decoding) so that the accuracy comparison in Section 6.6 is deterministic under identical inputs.

verification.spec: Configure the serving system with decoding temperature=0. Send the same prompt twice through the TokenDance serving pipeline in independent runs and assert the two generated outputs are token-for-token identical. Additionally, inspect the SamplingParams passed to the underlying vLLM engine and assert temperature == 0.0 exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to sweep number of agents (1-20) and offered QPS (1-16) as configurable experiment parameters, matching the parameter ranges used in Sections 6.2 and 6.3.

verification.spec: Invoke the experiment driver with `--num_agents 3 --qps 4` and again with `--num_agents 20 --qps 16`; assert both accept the arguments, log the configured values matching the request, and produce output artifacts distinguishable by parameter.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to record per-agent round latency, peak KV cache footprint, and restore latency per experiment run and emit them in a machine-readable form that the evaluation scripts can consume.

verification.spec: Run a short experiment and check the output file (e.g., JSON or CSV). Assert it contains per-agent round latency in ms, peak KV cache footprint in bytes/GiB, and restore latency per Mirror in ms, all parseable programmatically.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three baselines (vLLM with prefix caching, CacheBlend Ordinary Path without per-request recovery, and CacheBlend with full per-request PIC recovery) are configured and runnable on the same models and traces as TokenDance.
Baseline 1 (vLLM with prefix caching) is set up as a request-local reuse baseline.

Code has been implemented to launch a vLLM serving instance with prefix caching enabled (enable_prefix_caching=True) using the same Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B models used by TokenDance on the same A100 80GB GPU.

verification.spec: Verify a script/config exists (e.g., `baselines/vllm_prefix.sh` or Python driver) that launches vLLM with `enable_prefix_caching=True` for Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B on a single A100 80GB. Launch each and confirm the server starts, reports prefix caching enabled in logs, and accepts a test completion request.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to feed the same GenerativeAgents and AgentSociety replay traces used for TokenDance into the vLLM prefix-caching baseline, issuing each agent subrequest as an independent request without <TTSEP> separators.

verification.spec: Verify existence of a trace-replay driver that reads GenerativeAgents and AgentSociety traces and dispatches each agent subrequest as an independent HTTP/gRPC request to the vLLM prefix-caching server, WITHOUT any <TTSEP> separator tokens in the prompt. Inspect the code path and confirm that the prompt assembly for the baseline strips or omits TTSEP. Run a small trace (2 rounds, 3 agents) and log outgoing prompts to confirm no TTSEP is present.

sub_tasks.requirements: The vLLM prefix-caching baseline correctly reuses cached tokens only when a new request shares an exact token prefix with a stored sequence, and does not perform any position-independent or cross-prefix reuse.

verification.spec: Send two requests to the vLLM prefix-caching baseline: (1) prompt A = 'shared_prefix + private_history1 + shared_block'; (2) prompt B = 'shared_prefix + private_history2 + shared_block' where private_history1 and private_history2 differ in length. Query vLLM's prefix cache hit metrics. Verify that only the common prefix (up to the point of divergence) registers as a cache hit, and that the 'shared_block' appearing at different absolute positions does NOT produce any hit. Also verify no PIC/RoPE-correction path is invoked (no relevant log entries).

sub_tasks.requirements: Baseline 2 (CacheBlend Ordinary Path) is configured as a CPU-side KV cache pool without per-request cross-prefix recovery.
Code has been implemented to launch a CacheBlend-based serving stack (LMCache + vLLM) with the Ordinary Path enabled, providing a CPU-side KV cache pool but with per-request PIC recovery disabled.

verification.spec: Verify a launch script exists that starts LMCache + vLLM with the CacheBlend Ordinary Path configuration: LMCache-backed CPU KV cache pool enabled, but CacheBlend's per-request PIC recovery (RoPE correction + selective recomputation) explicitly disabled via config flag. Start the server, issue a test request, and inspect logs/config dump to confirm PIC recovery is off but the CPU KV pool is active.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CacheBlend Ordinary Path baseline does not perform RoPE-based positional correction or important-position selection for shared blocks at non-prefix offsets, matching the description of Ordinary Path in Section 6.1.

verification.spec: Instrument the CacheBlend Ordinary Path baseline to log invocations of the RoPE correction kernel and important-position selection routine. Send an All-Gather-style request where a shared block appears at a non-prefix offset. Verify (a) no RoPE correction is invoked for the shared block at the non-prefix offset, (b) no important-position selection is invoked, and (c) the shared block is either recomputed from scratch or only reused via exact prefix match.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to run the CacheBlend Ordinary Path baseline on the same Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B models and on both GenerativeAgents and AgentSociety traces used by TokenDance.

verification.spec: Verify launch/replay scripts exist that run CacheBlend Ordinary Path with Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen/Qwen2.5-14B on both GenerativeAgents and AgentSociety traces. Execute each of the four combinations for a short 2-round smoke test and confirm the runs complete and produce per-request latency logs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Baseline 3 (CacheBlend with full per-request PIC recovery) is configured as a per-request position-independent caching baseline.

Code has been implemented to enable CacheBlend's full per-request PIC recovery path, including RoPE rotation of cached keys, key-difference computation on the check layer, and selective recomputation of important positions for each request independently.

verification.spec: Verify a config exists that enables the full CacheBlend PIC path: RoPE rotation of cached K, key-difference computation on a configured check layer, and selective recomputation of important positions per request. Launch the server, send a request with a shared block at a non-prefix offset, and confirm via instrumentation that all three stages (RoPE, key-diff on check layer, selective recompute) execute for that request.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CacheBlend PIC baseline processes each request independently: for an N-agent All-Gather round it triggers N separate reuse passes (RoPE + important-position selection + selective recompute) over the shared blocks, without any collective grouping across requests.

verification.spec: Instrument the CacheBlend PIC baseline to count invocations of RoPE rotation and important-position selection per scheduler step. Submit an All-Gather round with N=5 agents sharing the same output block. Verify that the RoPE rotation kernel is invoked exactly 5 times (once per request) and important-position selection also 5 times, with no evidence of batched/grouped execution across the 5 requests.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to run CacheBlend with full per-request PIC recovery on Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B and on both GenerativeAgents and AgentSociety traces, using the same tokenizer, prompt content, and round structure as TokenDance (minus <TTSEP> block boundaries).

verification.spec: Verify replay scripts run CacheBlend with full per-request PIC on Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B, on both GenerativeAgents and AgentSociety traces. Confirm that the prompts sent to the baseline use the same tokenizer and same content as TokenDance except with <TTSEP> tokens stripped. Execute a 2-round smoke test for each of the four combinations and confirm completion with per-request latency logs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CacheBlend PIC baseline uses the same check-layer, important-position selection threshold, and selective recomputation policy as the CacheBlend backend that TokenDance uses internally, so any output-fidelity comparison isolates the collective/storage layer rather than PIC hyperparameters.

verification.spec: Dump the CacheBlend hyperparameter configuration (check layer index, important-position selection threshold / top-k ratio, recomputation policy) used by (a) the CacheBlend PIC baseline and (b) the CacheBlend backend inside TokenDance. Verify the two configurations are byte-identical for these hyperparameters via a diff of the config files or a printed config dictionary.

sub_tasks.requirements: The three baselines are integrated into a common harness that produces the metrics required by the evaluation.

Code has been implemented to sweep, for every baseline, agent counts from 1 to 10 and offered QPS from 1 to 16 on both workloads and both models, recording per-round latency, peak KV cache footprint, and restore overhead.

verification.spec: Verify a sweep driver exists that iterates agent counts {1..10} x QPS {1,2,4,8,12,16} x workloads {GenerativeAgents, AgentSociety} x models {Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-14B} for every baseline. Run a small subset (e.g., 2 agents x QPS {1,4} for one workload/model per baseline) as a smoke test and confirm the driver records per-round latency, peak KV cache footprint, and restore overhead to a structured output file (CSV/JSON).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute, from each baseline's latency sweep, (a) the maximum number of agents kept below the 1500 ms round-latency SLO and (b) the maximum number of agents sustainable at each QPS below that SLO.

verification.spec: Feed a synthetic latency-sweep CSV (agent_count, QPS, latency_ms) to the analysis script. Verify it outputs (a) max agents with latency<=1500ms per system and (b) max agents sustained at each QPS below 1500ms. Test with a hand-constructed CSV whose correct answers are known (e.g., latencies=1000ms for agents<=5 and 2000ms for agents>=6 should yield max_agents=5) and confirm the script returns those values exactly.

sub_tasks.requirements: All three baselines and TokenDance share the same underlying vLLM version, tokenizer, sampling configuration (temperature=0 for accuracy runs), and hardware (single A100 80 GB), so that comparisons in Figures 10, 11, 13, and 14 are apples-to-apples.

verification.spec: For each of the four systems (vLLM prefix, CacheBlend Ordinary, CacheBlend PIC, TokenDance), print/log at launch: vLLM version (pip show vllm), tokenizer name+hash, sampling config (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), and torch.cuda.get_device_name(0). Assert programmatically that vLLM version strings are identical, tokenizer hashes match, sampling config dicts are equal, and GPU device is 'NVIDIA A100 80GB'.

sub_tasks.requirements: On GenerativeAgents/Qwen2.5-14B at QPS=10, the vLLM prefix-caching baseline's round latency exceeds the 1500 ms SLO at approximately 7.5 agents, matching the crossing point reported in Section 6.2.

verification.spec: Run vLLM prefix-caching baseline on GenerativeAgents/Qwen2.5-14B at QPS=10, sweeping agent count from 1 to 10. Fit or linearly interpolate the round-latency-vs-agent-count curve and find the agent count at which latency first crosses 1500 ms. Verify the crossing occurs at approximately 7.5 agents.

sub_tasks.requirements: On GenerativeAgents/Qwen2.5-7B at QPS=16, the CacheBlend baseline supports approximately 4 agents and the vLLM prefix-caching baseline supports approximately 2 agents under the 1500 ms SLO, matching the numbers reported in Section 6.2.

verification.spec: Run CacheBlend PIC baseline and vLLM prefix-caching baseline on GenerativeAgents/Qwen2.5-7B at QPS=16, sweeping agent count. Compute the max agent count with round latency below 1500 ms for each. Verify CacheBlend supports ~4 agents (tolerance +/-1) and vLLM supports ~2 agents (tolerance +/-1).

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduce Figure 11: collective KV Cache reuse speedup over per-request serial PIC across agent counts (3, 5, 10, 15, 20) and QPS levels (1-16) on the GenerativeAgents workload, including the peak 2.57x at 10 agents/QPS=1 and >1.0x across all configurations.
The experiment harness for measuring collective vs. serial PIC reuse speedup on a GenerativeAgents round is implemented.

Code has been implemented to replay a single GenerativeAgents All-Gather round in which all agents share the same set of output blocks from the previous round, so that the degree of cross-agent redundancy is fixed and controlled across trials.

verification.spec: Inspect the replay harness: verify there is a function that constructs one All-Gather round in which every agent's prompt embeds the exact same set of shared output blocks (identical token sequences and block IDs) from a fixed previous-round record, so redundancy across agents is 100% controlled independent of agent count.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to sweep the number of agents in the replayed round over the exact set {3, 5, 10, 15, 20} while keeping the underlying shared output blocks identical.

verification.spec: Verify the sweep driver iterates agent counts over exactly {3, 5, 10, 15, 20} and, for each, replicates the identical shared output blocks to all agents so the underlying content is unchanged as N varies.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to sweep the offered QPS over the exact set {1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16} for each agent count, driving requests into the serving engine at the target arrival rate.

verification.spec: Verify the load generator iterates offered QPS over exactly {1, 2, 4, 8, 12, 16} for each agent count and injects requests into the serving engine at the target Poisson or fixed-rate arrival to match target QPS.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been configured to run this experiment on an NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU using Qwen2.5-7B as the serving model, matching the Section 6.3 setup on GenerativeAgents.

verification.spec: Verify experiment config declares device=NVIDIA A100 80GB and model=Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B for the Section 6.3 (Figure 11) collective-reuse speedup experiment on GenerativeAgents, and that torch.cuda.get_device_name reports an A100 80GB at runtime.

sub_tasks.requirements: The serial per-request PIC baseline against which speedup is measured is implemented and instrumented.

Code has been implemented for a serial PIC reuse path in which each of the N requests in the round independently invokes the CacheBlend-style PIC backend (RoPE rotation, key-diff, important-position selection, selective recomputation) with no cross-request grouping.

verification.spec: Inspect the serial PIC path implementation: for each of the N requests it independently invokes the CacheBlend-style routine performing RoPE rotation, key-diff computation, important-position selection, and selective recomputation, with no batching or grouping across requests. Confirm no shared tensors span the N calls.

sub_tasks.requirements: For an N-agent round on the serial PIC path, the reuse analysis (RoPE rotation and important-position selection) is executed N times (once per request), and this can be verified via kernel counters or instrumentation.

verification.spec: Instrument the RoPE-rotation kernel and important-position-selection kernel with call counters. Run one N-agent round on the serial PIC path for N in {3,5,10} and verify each counter equals N * layers (or the analogous per-request count).

sub_tasks.requirements: The TokenDance collective KV Cache reuse path used as the speedup numerator is correctly wired for this experiment.

Code has been implemented so that, for each replayed round in the sweep, the KV Collector groups all N compatible requests (same active prompt length, same cached span, non-overlapping slot maps) and drives them through a single collective reuse pass.

verification.spec: Add logging inside the KV Collector's grouping logic. Run a replayed round with N compatible requests (matching active prompt length, cached span, non-overlapping slot maps) and verify a single group of size N is formed and a single collective reuse pass is invoked (not N passes).

sub_tasks.requirements: On the collective path, RoPE rotation is applied once per layer to the concatenated Q/K tensors of the group and important-position selection is performed once per layer on the check layer for the whole group, rather than once per request.

verification.spec: Instrument the RoPE call and important-position-selection call on the collective path. For an N-agent group, verify RoPE is invoked once per layer on a concatenated Q/K tensor of batch dimension N, and important-position selection runs once per layer on the check layer for the whole group.

sub_tasks.requirements: The collective path uses the same CacheBlend selective-recomputation backend for per-position correction as the serial baseline, so the two paths differ only in whether reuse analysis is amortized across the group.

verification.spec: Inspect the code: verify the collective path calls into the same CacheBlend selective-recomputation module (same function/class) as the serial baseline for per-position K/V correction, and that the only structural difference is the grouping/amortization layer above it.

sub_tasks.requirements: Latency measurement and speedup computation are implemented consistently with Figure 11.
Code has been implemented to measure end-to-end prefill/reuse latency of one All-Gather round on both the serial PIC path and the collective path under identical inputs and warm caches.

verification.spec: Verify a benchmark harness exists that, given identical inputs and warm KV caches, runs one All-Gather round through (a) the serial PIC path and (b) the collective path, measuring end-to-end prefill+reuse latency for each and returning both times.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute speedup = (serial PIC round latency) / (collective reuse round latency) for each (agent_count, QPS) cell and report it as the Figure 11 y-axis value.

verification.spec: Verify the analysis script computes speedup = t_serial / t_collective per (agent_count, QPS) cell and produces a table/dataframe with columns {agent_count, qps, speedup} used as Figure 11 y-axis.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to plot speedup vs. QPS with one line per agent count in {3, 5, 10, 15, 20}, reproducing the structure of Figure 11 including a horizontal reference at 1.0x.

verification.spec: Run the plotting script and verify it produces a figure with speedup on the y-axis vs QPS on the x-axis, one line per agent count in {3,5,10,15,20}, and a horizontal dashed/solid reference line at y=1.0.

sub_tasks.requirements: The specific numerical claims in Section 6.3 / Figure 11 are reproduced.
At 10 agents and QPS=1 on GenerativeAgents, the measured collective-vs-serial-PIC speedup matches the reported peak of 2.57x.

verification.spec: On GenerativeAgents replay with Qwen2.5-7B on A100-80GB, measure collective-reuse speedup over serial PIC at N=10 agents, QPS=1. Verify value matches 2.57x.

sub_tasks.requirements: At 5 agents and QPS=1, the measured speedup matches the reported 1.31x.

verification.spec: On GenerativeAgents replay with Qwen2.5-7B on A100-80GB, measure collective-reuse speedup over serial PIC at N=5 agents, QPS=1. Verify value matches 1.31x.

sub_tasks.requirements: At 3 agents and QPS=1, the measured speedup matches the reported 1.17x.

verification.spec: On GenerativeAgents replay with Qwen2.5-7B on A100-80GB, measure collective-reuse speedup over serial PIC at N=3 agents, QPS=1. Verify value matches 1.17x.

sub_tasks.requirements: At 15 agents and QPS=1, the measured speedup matches the reported 1.61x.

verification.spec: Run one GenerativeAgents round with 15 agents at QPS=1 on Qwen2.5-7B. Measure the per-round prefill/reuse latency for TokenDance's collective KV Cache reuse path and for a serial per-request PIC (CacheBlend) baseline under identical inputs. Compute speedup = latency_serial / latency_collective and compare to 1.61x.

sub_tasks.requirements: At 20 agents and QPS=1, the measured speedup matches the reported 1.73x.

verification.spec: Run one GenerativeAgents round with 20 agents at QPS=1 on Qwen2.5-7B. Measure prefill/reuse latency for collective KV Cache reuse and for per-request serial PIC baseline. Compute speedup ratio and compare to 1.73x.

sub_tasks.requirements: Across every (agent_count, QPS) cell in the sweep (agents in {3,5,10,15,20}, QPS in {1,2,4,8,12,16}), the measured collective-reuse speedup is strictly greater than 1.0x.

verification.spec: Run the full GenerativeAgents sweep over agent_count in {3,5,10,15,20} x QPS in {1,2,4,8,12,16} on Qwen2.5-7B, measuring collective-reuse speedup vs serial per-request PIC in each cell. Assert every cell's measured speedup is > 1.0x.

sub_tasks.requirements: For QPS > 4, the speedups across agent counts converge into approximately the 1.2x-1.6x range as reported in Section 6.3.

verification.spec: From the same sweep, extract speedup values at QPS in {8,12,16} across agent counts {3,5,10,15,20}. Verify that the mean speedup at these high-QPS cells falls into approximately 1.2x-1.6x and the spread across agent counts narrows compared to QPS=1.

sub_tasks.requirements: At QPS=16, the measured collective-reuse speedup lies within the reported 1.3x-1.5x band across agent counts.

verification.spec: At QPS=16, measure collective-reuse speedup vs serial PIC across agent counts {3,5,10,15,20} on Qwen2.5-7B GenerativeAgents. Verify all measured values are within roughly the 1.3x-1.5x band.

sub_tasks.requirements: At low QPS (QPS=1), the speedup increases monotonically from 3 to 10 agents and then decreases from 10 to 20 agents, reproducing the peak-at-10 shape described in Section 6.3.

verification.spec: At QPS=1, collect speedup values for agent counts {3,5,10,15,20}. Assert speedup(3) < speedup(5) < speedup(10) and speedup(10) > speedup(15) > speedup(20), reproducing the peak-at-10-agents unimodal shape.

depends_on: Baselines: vLLM Prefix Caching and CacheBlend Variants

sub_tasks.requirements: The redundancy characterization of recovered KV Caches is reproduced (Section 6.4, Figure 12), including block-sparse compression ratios of 11.2x on Qwen2.5-7B and 17.5x on Qwen2.5-14B, and the average per-Mirror changed-block counts of 53.2 (7B) and 59.6 (14B) blocks in a single GenerativeAgents round.
The experimental scaffold that produces recovered KV Caches for a single GenerativeAgents round and characterizes cross-agent redundancy at block granularity is in place.

Code has been implemented to load a single GenerativeAgents round trace containing a group of All-Gather agent subrequests that share the same set of previous-round output blocks, matching the setup used to characterize KV Cache redundancy in Section 6.4.

verification.spec: Verify that a loader function exists and, when invoked, returns a set of All-Gather agent subrequests from one GenerativeAgents round in which every subrequest's prompt contains the identical set of previous-round output blocks (only the private history differs). Check that the returned structure exposes per-agent prompts and the shared block set.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the redundancy characterization for both Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B under identical GenerativeAgents round inputs, producing the two model conditions shown in Figure 12.

verification.spec: Verify that a redundancy-characterization driver can be run with model='Qwen2.5-7B' and model='Qwen2.5-14B' using the same GenerativeAgents round input, and that both invocations produce compression-ratio and average-changed-block outputs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented so that the KV Cache block size used for redundancy analysis is 32 tokens per block (matching the '32 tokens per block' granularity stated in Section 6.4), and the same block size is used for both models.

verification.spec: Inspect the configuration used by the redundancy-characterization code and assert that the KV Cache block size is 32 tokens for both Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen2.5-14B runs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to produce the recovered per-agent KV Caches for the target round using the collective KV Cache reuse path (with CacheBlend-style PIC recovery as the backend), so that the analyzed caches are the post-reuse recovered caches rather than freshly recomputed dense caches.

verification.spec: Trace or instrument the pipeline that produces the per-agent KV Caches analyzed in Section 6.4. Verify that (a) the KV Collector's collective reuse path is invoked for the round, (b) the PIC backend used is CacheBlend-style selective recomputation, and (c) the caches passed to the redundancy analyzer are the post-reuse recovered caches (contain both reused-from-cache tokens and selectively recomputed positions), not freshly full recomputations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Master selection and Mirror diff extraction over the round's recovered KV Caches are implemented so that the compression ratio and changed-block counts can be measured.

Code has been implemented to select the Master cache within the round using the reuse-plan output from KV Collector (the request with the lowest accumulated per-request deviation among the group), consistent with the Master-selection rule described in Sections 4.2 and 4.3.

verification.spec: Instrument the KV Collector's reuse-plan output and verify that the request selected as Master is the one with the lowest accumulated per-request deviation score among the group. Confirm on a synthetic round with known deviation scores that Master selection matches the argmin rule.

Finally, get() on both entries returns semantically correct results.

Also assert that a fixed-size-chunk hasher (baseline) produces different keys for the two SHARED occurrences, confirming the segment hasher is doing offset-independent matching.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Autellix-style agent-aware scheduling is available as a baseline scheduler, dispatching multi-agent subrequests according to application-level dependency graphs (prioritizing critical requests to reduce head-of-line blocking) while leaving KV Cache computation and storage untouched.

verification.spec: Import the Autellix baseline scheduler module; instantiate with a synthetic multi-agent dependency graph containing one critical path and several non-critical branches; submit a burst of requests and assert that critical-path requests are dispatched before non-critical ones (ordering check on dispatch log). Also assert that per-request KV Cache objects remain independent (no cross-request sharing) after execution.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that Tokencake KV-cache-centric agent-aware scheduling is available as a baseline that proactively offloads stalled agents and reserves memory for critical agents on top of a standard KV-cache backend.

verification.spec: Import the Tokencake baseline; simulate a multi-agent workload where one agent stalls (awaits external input) while others are active; assert that the stalled agent's KV Cache is offloaded (moved out of GPU pool) within a bounded number of scheduler ticks, and that the offload event is recorded in the scheduler log.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that SGLang-style prefix caching is available as a baseline: KV Cache entries are reused only when a new request shares an exact token prefix with a stored sequence starting from position zero.

verification.spec: Instantiate the SGLang prefix-cache baseline; submit two requests where request B shares a 100-token prefix with request A but diverges at token 101; assert that only the shared prefix is reused (cache hit length == 100) and that no reuse occurs for the divergent tail. Then submit a request whose shared block appears at a non-zero offset; assert cache hit length == 0.
verification.paper_cite: Section 2.2 (Prefix caching, used by vLLM and SGLang)

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that EPIC position-independent caching is available as a baseline that can reuse KV Cache blocks at arbitrary positional offsets by applying RoPE correction.

verification.spec: Instantiate the EPIC baseline; cache a block B at position 0-31 from request A; submit request B where the same content block appears at position 100-131. Assert that EPIC applies RoPE rotation to align cached keys with new positions and returns a non-empty reuse for that block. Verify the corrected keys match freshly-computed keys within tolerance 1e-2 (mean absolute error).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that KVLink position-independent caching is available as a baseline that recovers cross-request reuse at arbitrary positions through position correction.

verification.spec: Instantiate KVLink baseline; cache blocks from a source request; submit a target request containing the same content at a shifted offset. Assert KVLink returns a corrected KV cache for the shared blocks and that the pipeline processes each request independently (per-request analysis, not collective grouping).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that KVComm cross-context KV cache communication is available as a baseline for online cross-context KV-cache transfer between LLM agents.

verification.spec: Instantiate the KVComm baseline; set up two agents where agent-2's prompt reuses part of agent-1's context. Assert KVComm transfers the relevant KV blocks between the two agent contexts and that the transfer preserves standard per-request KV cache semantics (each request still owns a full dense cache post-transfer).

verification.spec: Run the collective-reuse-only ablation on the GenerativeAgents replay with 10 agents at QPS=1, measure prefill speedup vs. serial per-request PIC baseline; assert measured_speedup >= 1.5 (paper reports 2.57x peak, so 1.5x is a conservative lower bound accounting for the disabled storage optimization).

verification.spec: Run per-request PIC recovery to produce recovered KV Caches for one GenerativeAgents round on Qwen2.5-7B; encode the resulting caches with the Master-Mirror block-sparse diff representation; compute compression_ratio = sum(full_cache_sizes) / (master_size + sum(diff_sizes)); assert |measured - 11.2| / 11.2 <= 0.25.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that an ablation compares fused diff restore against dense restore (which materializes a full Mirror by copying the Master and overwriting differing blocks); fused restore achieves >=1.3x speedup over dense restore at 10 agents on GenerativeAgents/Qwen2.5-7B.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that when no explicit reuse plan is provided (e.g. request arrives outside a recognized All-Gather round), the diff-aware storage backend falls back to a token-similarity heuristic to select a Master among existing cached entries.

verification.spec: Populate the storage backend with several cached entries whose token overlaps with a new incoming request vary. Call the store path for the new request WITHOUT providing a reuse plan. Assert that the backend invokes the token-similarity heuristic (verified via a logged / mocked call) and selects the cached entry with the highest token overlap as Master. Assert the Mirror diff size is proportional to (1 - overlap_fraction).
verification.paper_cite: Section 4.3 (fallback to token-similarity heuristic); Section 5 (Diff-Aware Storage)
